work.text: From 1681 to 1684, Bada treated painting as an outlet for his emotions, particularly his dissatisfaction with his second marriage. He expanded his repertoire of subjects to include animals like birds and fish in addition to flowers and vegetables.

After leaving the priesthood, from 1680 to 1684, he invented new names while keeping the name Geshan. Most of his new names contained the word lu, meaning donkey, a condescending descriptor for a Buddhist monk.

moment.text: During this time, Bada also showed signs of eccentric behavior. Many believed he was feigning madness to eschew political involvement.

matters.text: Whatever the case, the marriage was short-lived, and more specific messages about it were expressed through the writings on his paintings and works of calligraphy between late 1682 and 1684.

source.author: Joseph Chang
source.title: The Life and Painting of Bada Shanren, in In Pursuit of Heavenly Harmony: Paintings and Calligraphy by Bada Shanren
source.publisher: Freer Gallery of Art and Arthur M. Sackler Gallery, Smithsonian Institution (Internet Archive scan)

matters.text: Bada's work during the 1680s were imbued with personal emotions and political sentiments. His animal subjects often wore human-like expressions.
